title: Rescuing Specific Exception Types
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of rescuing specific exception types in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply rescuing specific exception types in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to avoiding accidental suppression of errors and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Rescuing Specific Exception Types through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding rescuing specific exception types helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Rescuing Specific Exception Types helps you reason about multiple rescue branches. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Multiple rescue branches. Then connect it to Rescue ordering. The remaining syllabus points—Avoiding accidental suppression of errors—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Rescuing Specific Exception Types
content_blocks.code:
begin
  Integer("12x")
rescue ArgumentError
  puts "Please enter a whole number."
end

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports rescuing specific exception types. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.text: Create a second example for rescuing specific exception types using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Avoiding accidental suppression of errors), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.
